title: Seven-season GJ 176 fits do not resolve a change in the 8.776-day wave under four shared-sign error models
abstract: We test seasonal changes in two known GJ 176 velocity waves with 115 public HARPS-RVBank version 02 visits in seven seasons. Joint sine fits use free season means and fixed periods. The 8.776-day wave gives a loss reduction of 10.008 for 12 added coefficients. Four shared-sign error models give upper-tail fractions of 0.7015 to 0.7940. They do not resolve a change. Under a stated Gaussian sensitivity model, a 2 m/s late change is detected in only 12 of 200 trials. The 39.34-day wave gives a larger loss reduction, but its fraction rises from 0.0005 for one-day bins to 0.3285 for 100-day bins. Thus its apparent change depends on the error model. Period and extraction controls show further limits. No new planet, physical cause, or independent observation is established. The external source database is excluded. Code, aggregate results, figures, exact source provenance, a hash-checked retrieval script and repeat steps are included. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-78e2230b6ed8; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.
